title: Microscopy and Microanalysis in Modern Engineering Materials and Additive Manufacturing Education
content: The fourth industrial revolution, Industry 4.0 (I4.0), has had a massive impact on Engineering education and its delivery over the last decade. I4.0, which involves the digitisation of manufacturing, has led to the inclusion of topics such as Additive Manufacturing (AM), Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI), into university curricula. Industry 5.0 (I5.0), however, is already here and calls for further modernisation of both engineering units and how they may be taught. In contrast to I4.0 which is technology focused, I5.0 stipulates that the implementation of technology needs to be human-centric, resilient and sustainable [1]. In Europe, a key focus for I5.0 has also been identified as achieving the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) [2]. These I5.0 concepts and goals therefore cover not only industry and engineering, but all of society in general.
